entries.name: Great Pyramid of Giza
entries.purpose: tomb of pharaoh Khufu; a statement of divine kingship
parts: four triangular faces aligned to the cardinals
layout: a 230 block square of smooth stone
rising 146 blocks to a flat summit platform
two smaller pyramids and the Sphinx flank it nearby
entries.found: one; the largest of three pyramids on the Giza plateau west of the Nile
entries.notes: Current height is about 139 m after the casing was stripped. The tallest human structure for over 3,700 years; model it as a rare desert landmark.

entries.name: Taj Mahal
entries.purpose: mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal; monumental display of Mughal love and power
parts: central onion dome on a drum
layout: a white cube-like mausoleum on a low plinth
four minarets at the plinth corners
long reflecting pool axis to the south
entries.found: one, at Agra on the Yamuna river
entries.notes: Perfectly symmetrical; symmetry breaking only in the two cenotaphs inside. Glows at dawn and dusk; the garden and pool are as important as the building.

entries.name: Stonehenge
entries.purpose: ceremonial and ritual center; aligned on the solstices; cremation burial ground
layout: a circular earthwork enclosure about 110 blocks across
an inner ring of sarsens capped with lintels
a horseshoe of trilithons opening northeast toward the heel stone
entries.found: one, on Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire (inspired stone circles exist across Britain)
entries.notes: Silhouette is everything: post and lintel, not solid mass. Built in stages over 1,500 years; midsummer sunrise alignment is the classic hook for a solstice event.

entries.name: Colosseum (Flavian Amphitheatre)
entries.purpose: public amphitheater for games, executions and spectacle
layout: a free-standing ellipse, about 189 by 156 blocks
concentric arcades rising 48 blocks
a sunken arena with trapdoors and cages below
entries.found: one, in central Rome; ~50,000 seat capacity
entries.notes: The outer wall is largely ruined on one side; broken silhouette reads instantly as Rome. Largest amphitheater ever built.

entries.name: Parthenon
entries.purpose: temple to Athena Parthenos; Athenian treasury; victory monument
parts: peripteral colonnade of 8 by 17 Doric columns
cella housing the Athena Parthenos statue
layout: a rectangular marble platform about 70 by 31 blocks
a colonnade all around, swelling subtly (all lines curve)
a pedimented gable at each end
entries.found: one, on the Acropolis of Athens
entries.notes: Every line is slightly curved; a perfectly straight voxel build looks wrong to any classically trained eye. Roof lost since 1687.

entries.name: Angkor Wat
entries.purpose: state temple-mountain of Suryavarman II; dedicated to Vishnu; later Buddhist
parts: Churning of the Sea of Milk bas-relief
layout: a vast moated rectangle aligned to the equinox
concentric walled enclosures rising to a central tower
a central tower ringed by four smaller towers
entries.found: one, at Angkor in Cambodia; the largest religious monument ever built
entries.notes: Built to represent Mount Meru, the Hindu cosmic mountain. Moat and causeway mean the visitor crosses water before stone; the temple reads best from across the moat.

entries.name: Hagia Sophia
entries.purpose: cathedral of Constantinople; imperial mosque from 1453; now a mosque
parts: central dome, 31 m diameter on pendentives
layout: a vast domed basilica nave flanked by side aisles
minarets at the corners after Ottoman conversion
the dome floats on a ring of light
entries.found: one, in Istanbul
entries.notes: Built in under six years; the largest interior space in Europe for nearly a thousand years. The dome-on-pendentives trick defined church building forever.

entries.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
entries.purpose: cathedral of the Catholic archdiocese of Paris
parts: spire reaching 96 m after the 2019 fire
layout: a Latin cross basilica about 130 blocks long on the Île de la Cité
twin towers flat-roofed at the west front
a spire over the crossing
entries.found: one, on the Île de la Cité, Paris
entries.notes: The 2019 fire and rebuild are part of the story now; the new spire repeats Viollet-le-Duc's 96 m design. Flying buttresses let the walls be glass.

entries.name: St. Peter's Basilica
entries.purpose: papal basilica over the tomb of St Peter; spiritual heart of Catholicism
parts: Michelangelo's dome, 136.6 m to the lantern
longest church interior in the world
piazza with colonnade embracing the square
layout: a huge basilica attached to a keyhole piazza and colonnade
a great central dome over the crossing
the piazza opens to a welcoming oval of columns
entries.found: one, at the Vatican, Rome
entries.notes: Dome exterior 137 m; dome interior 118.6 m. Bernini's colonnade arms are the counter-Reformation welcoming the world.

entries.name: The Kaaba (Masjid al-Haram)
entries.era: pre-Islamic; rebuilt many times (current form largely 1040 CE)
entries.purpose: holiest site in Islam; the qibla toward which all Muslims pray
parts: Black Stone in the eastern corner
layout: a near-cube of stone, 13 blocks tall, draped in black cloth
the vast circular courtyard of Masjid al-Haram wraps around it
pilgrims circle it seven times during hajj and umrah
entries.found: one, in Mecca, Saudi Arabia
entries.notes: Visited by over a million hajj pilgrims per year; at its busiest the courtyard holds millions. The door is raised against floods; the kiswah is replaced annually.

entries.name: Dome of the Rock
entries.purpose: shrine marking the Foundation Stone, sacred to Islam, Judaism and Christianity
layout: an octagonal shrine capped by a golden dome
two concentric ambulatories around the central rock
four cardinal entrances
entries.found: one, on the Temple Mount, Jerusalem
entries.notes: The oldest surviving major Islamic building (691 CE). Not a mosque; a shrine. The golden dome dominates every Jerusalem skyline view.

entries.name: Sagrada Família
entries.purpose: Expiatory Temple of the Holy Family; ongoing work of devotion
layout: a basílica in plan, but built like a stone forest
spires that look like sandcastles and basalt
facade sculptures that shift from joy to suffering to glory
entries.found: one, in Barcelona
entries.notes: Begun 1882 and still unfinished; Gaudí died in 1926. Designed one metre shorter than Montjuïc so God's work stays taller than man's.

entries.name: Mount Rushmore
entries.purpose: national memorial to four US presidents; economic revival of the Black Hills
parts: heads of Washington, Jefferson, Roosevelt and Lincoln
unfinished Hall of Records behind the faces
layout: a granite cliff face carved into four presidential portraits
faces sized to be read from the valley below
entries.found: one, in the Black Hills of South Dakota
entries.notes: Carved by Gutzon Borglum and his son. Built on land sacred to the Lakota; the contrast is worth flagging in game lore.

entries.name: Statue of Liberty
entries.purpose: gift from France celebrating liberty and the friendship of two republics
layout: a copper colossus on a granite pedestal on Liberty Island
93 m total height; statue alone is 46 m
visible from the harbor mouth
entries.found: one, at the entrance of New York Harbor
entries.notes: Copper skin over a steel armature; turned green within a generation. First thing millions of immigrants saw; the game's 'harbor wonder'.

entries.name: Arc de Triomphe
entries.purpose: celebrate Napoleon's victories; memorial to French soldiers
parts: Names of 158 battles on the inner walls
Tomb of the Unknown Soldier (1921) with eternal flame
layout: a freestanding triumphal arch at the center of the Étoile, twelve radiating avenues
50 blocks tall, 45 wide
parade route passes directly through the arch
entries.found: one, at the Place Charles de Gaulle, Paris
entries.notes: Chalgrin's design, completed after Napoleon. The twelve-avenue star junction is a strong urban-planning motif for a French-style city.

entries.name: Christ the Redeemer
entries.purpose: catholic monument overlooking Rio; New Seven Wonder of the World
parts: open-armed Art Deco Christ, 30 m tall
layout: a huge figure on a mountain crest above a steep city
arms outstretched 28 blocks across
view over the bay and the city below
entries.found: one, atop Corcovado, Rio de Janeiro
entries.notes: Total 38 m including pedestal; the mountain summit does the rest of the work. Lightning strikes it constantly; bring a rod.

entries.name: Washington Monument
materials: marble (three sources, visible as a color change line)
entries.purpose: memorial to George Washington; national ceremonial obelisk
parts: two doorways with empty door frames
layout: a stark white obelisk on the National Mall between the Lincoln and Jefferson memorials
a perfect axial marker
the reflected pool axis runs toward the Capitol
entries.found: one, on the National Mall, Washington DC
entries.notes: Height rung ten times the base width by design. The color change at 150 ft visibly marks the 1854 funding halt and 1879 restart.

entries.name: Machu Picchu
entries.purpose: Inca royal estate and religious retreat for Pachacuti
layout: a saddle between two green cones at 2,430 m
dry-stone walls keyed to seismic shake
terraced farms cascade off the slopes
entries.found: one, in the Urubamba valley, Peru; 'found' by Hiram Bingham in 1911, never lost to local farmers
entries.notes: Built without mortar; walls survive earthquakes that flatten modern buildings nearby. Cloud forest at the edges; condor country.

entries.name: Pyramid of the Sun
entries.purpose: largest pyramid of Teotihuacan; religious center of a city of 100,000
parts: Avenue of the Dead approach, 2.4 km
layout: a huge stepped pyramid aligned 15.5 degrees east of north
sits on an enormous 4-tiered urban grid
mountain-like silhouette above the Avenue of the Dead
entries.found: one, at Teotihuacan, Mexico, 50 km northeast of Mexico City
entries.notes: Name given by the Aztecs, who found the city abandoned; the builders' name is lost. Space enough for the Pyramid of Giza's base at 225 blocks across.

entries.name: El Castillo (Pyramid of Kukulcán)
entries.purpose: temple to Kukulcán; calendar monument; state cult center
parts: four stair cases of 91 steps each plus the top step = 365
serpent balustrades with feathered serpent heads
layout: a square step pyramid in a plaza, 55 blocks per side
four symmetric staircases
the plaza crowds around; not walkable inside since a shaft was sealed
entries.found: one, at Chichén Itzá, Yucatán, Mexico
entries.notes: Equinox shadows crawl down the balustrade like a serpent descending Kukulcán; a ready-made 'event' for a spring/autumn equinox tick in game.

entries.name: Al-Khazneh (The Treasury), Petra
entries.purpose: likely tomb of Nabataean king Aretas IV; facade for the royal cult
parts: Hellenistic facade carved from living rock, 40 m tall
broken pediment with a central tholos
two tiers of columns and figures
layout: a facade at the end of the narrow siq canyon, suddenly huge
reached only on foot through 1.2 km of slot canyon
viewed from a small plaza, feet above a dry torrent bed
entries.found: one, at Petra, Jordan; the valley holds hundreds of rock-cut facades
entries.notes: Not a building but a carving; perfect for a 'hidden wonder' reveal. The siq approach is cinematic; the view shocks on first sight.

entries.name: The Pantheon
entries.purpose: temple to all gods; now a Catholic basilica and royal tomb
parts: unreinforced concrete dome, 43.3 m span, exactly the height from floor
layout: a cylindrical drum behind a temple portico
the dome is a hemisphere sitting on the drum; sphere and cylinder interpenetrate
a single blazing eye in the roof
entries.found: one, in Rome; the best-preserved building from antiquity
entries.notes: Rain falls in through the oculus and drains through the floor. The largest masonry dome for 1,300 years; still unmatched in pure concrete.

entries.name: Great Sphinx of Giza
materials: carved out of a single limestone spur
entries.purpose: guardian of the Giza plateau; debated (Khafre's face or older?)
layout: a recumbent lion-human on a low causeway facing east
aligned roughly with the rising sun on the equinox
keystone-shaped natural spur, carved in place
entries.found: one, on the Giza plateau, Egypt
entries.notes: Nose gone since at least the 15th c. (gunpowder or erosion, still debated). Half-buried in sand for most of its life; the sand kept it alive.

entries.name: Abu Simbel (Great Temple)
materials: sandstone (carved from the cliff; moved 1964-68 onto an artificial hill)
entries.purpose: mortuary temple to Ramesses II; border show of force toward Nubia
parts: four seated colossi of Ramesses II, 20 m each
inner sanctuary with the sun-aligned cult statues
layout: a cliff-cut facade facing the Nile-turned-lake
interior cuts 65 m into solid rock
twice a year the sun lights the inner cult statues (Feb 22, Oct 22)
entries.found: one, on Lake Nasser, Egypt; raised 60 m in the 1960s to escape the dam
entries.notes: The relocation story (cut into 1,000-tonne blocks and reassembled) is a triumph of engineering movable monuments; a template for any 'king moved' quest.

entries.name: Karnak Temple (Great Hypostyle Hall)
entries.era: c. 1550 BCE onwards; hall c. 1290-1224 BCE
entries.purpose: cult temple of Amun; religious capital of ancient Egypt for 2,000 years
parts: 134 columns; 12 central columns ~21 m tall, 122 side ~13 m
obelisks of Thutmose I and Hatshepsut
layout: an enormous walled precinct with pylons (gateways) on an east-west axis
processional way to Luxor Temple 3 km away
the hall is a forest of columns, clerestory light above
entries.found: one, on the east bank of the Nile at Luxor (Thebes)
entries.notes: Largest room of any ancient building. Built and rebuilt by thirty pharaohs over a millennium and a half; archaeology as palimpsest.

entries.name: Ziggurat of Ur (Great Ziggurat)
entries.era: c. 2100 BCE; restored 6th c. BCE and in the 20th c.
entries.purpose: temple tower of the moon god Nanna; center of Ur's state cult
parts: triple stairways converging at a gate
baked-brick facade stamped with Ur-Nammu's name
layout: a stepped rectangular massif, 64 by 45 blocks
monumental stairways climbing the east face
summit temple reached only by priests
entries.found: one, at Tell el-Muqayyar, Iraq (near Nasiriyah); original height speculative
entries.notes: Height 30 m is an educated reconstruction; only the base survives. Mansions upon terraces; the blueprint for Babylon's Tower of Babel legend.

entries.name: Borobudur
entries.purpose: Buddhist monument; a three-dimensional mandala for pilgrimage and meditation
layout: a 123-block square base stepping up to a circular summit stupa
pilgrim walks clockwise up five square terraces and three circular ones
every relief must be read in sequence to complete the path
entries.found: one, in Central Java, Indonesia; largest Buddhist monument on Earth
entries.notes: Interior hidden foot (Kamadhatu) was concealed by the builders themselves. A 5 km circumambulation in stone; the ultimate 'walk the mandala' design pattern.

entries.name: Brihadeeswarar Temple (Big Temple), Thanjavur
entries.purpose: Shaivite temple built by Rajaraja Chola I; imperial statement of Chola power
parts: vimana tower, 66 m, capped by a single ~80 t granite block
layout: a vast walled courtyard centered on the granite vimana
the tower dominates the Kaveri plain for miles
monolithic Nandi faces the temple down the axis
entries.found: one, at Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, India
entries.notes: Built with no binding mortar; the 80 t capstone was raised up a 6 km earthen ramp. Dakshina Meru; Chola engineering at its peak.

entries.name: Great Stupa at Sanchi
entries.purpose: reliquary for the Buddha; circumambulation monument
parts: hemispherical anda dome, 36.6 m diameter, 16.5 m high
harmika and triple umbrella (chattra) on top
layout: a smooth dome on a drum, crowned by an umbrella
walked around clockwise, never entered
four gates at the cardinal points, dripping with carving
entries.found: one, on a hilltop at Sanchi, Madhya Pradesh, India; hundreds of smaller stupas dot the hill
entries.notes: The toranas carve Jataka tales in exuberant detail; the earliest great Buddhist stone sculpture. Dome first, details later — the shape does the meaning.

entries.name: Shwedagon Pagoda
entries.era: origins c. 6th-15th c.; gilded over centuries
materials: diamonds and rubies on the finial
entries.purpose: reliquary housing relics of four Buddhas; Burma's spiritual center
parts: terraces of smaller stupas and pavilions
layout: a vast gilded bell rising from a platform ringed by smaller shrines
fully gilded; the sun makes it a beacon
pilgrims shed shoes at the base and circle the stupa
entries.found: one, in Yangon, Myanmar
entries.notes: Covered in over 7,000 gold plates; the finial is topped by thousands of diamonds. Legend says King Okkalapa raised it 2,600 years ago; in truth it is at least 1,000 years old.

entries.name: Saint Basil's Cathedral
entries.purpose: votive church for Ivan the Terrible's capture of Kazan and Astrakhan
parts: nine chapels clustered around a central tent
onion domes in vivid swirled colors
layout: a bonfire of nine separate churches on one base, each with its own dome
asymmetric cluster, not one unified basilica
stands free on Red Square
entries.found: one, on Red Square, Moscow
entries.notes: Nine separate churches fused into one; the silhouette is a chaos of domes. Built to commemorate a siege; every dome differs. Nothing like it exists anywhere.

entries.name: Statue of Unity
entries.purpose: memorial to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, uniter of post-independence India
parts: viewing gallery in the chest, 153 m up
valley of flowers and memorial at the base
layout: a colossal standing figure on a river island pedestal
nearly twice the Statue of Liberty's height
visible from 40 km away
entries.found: one, near Kevadia, Gujarat, India
entries.notes: Tallest statue in the world. The Sardar enforced princely-state accession; the statue is a deliberate statement on national unity over separatism.

entries.name: Göbekli Tepe
materials: limestone (T-shaped pillars, up to 16 t, later 50 t)
entries.purpose: monumental ritual enclosures; oldest known temple complex
parts: T-shaped pillars carved with foxes, vultures, lions, snakes and scorpions
deliberately buried by its own builders around 8000 BCE
layout: a hilltop with layered circular enclosures
pillars up to 6 m tall arranged in rings
nothing like a house; this is a gathering place, not a dwelling
entries.found: one, near Şanlıurfa in southeastern Turkey; older than Stonehenge by 7,000 years
entries.notes: Built by hunter-gatherers before farming; religion may have driven settlement, not the reverse. The 'world's first temple'; redefines what a monument is.

entries.name: Newgrange
entries.purpose: passage tomb; solstice observatory; ancestral cult
parts: kidney-shaped mound, 85 m wide, 13 m high
19 m passage to a cruciform chamber
layout: a huge grassy dome on a low ridge above the Boyne
winter-solstice sunrise shines down the passage into the chamber
surrounded by 97 kerbstones; standing stones in front
entries.found: one, in County Meath, Ireland; part of the Brú na Bóinne UNESCO complex
entries.notes: Older than Stonehenge and the Great Pyramid. The roofbox lets the rising sun crawl the full 19 m of passage at dawn on the solstice; six minutes of light per year.

entries.name: Kailasa Temple, Ellora
materials: carved directly out of solid basalt cliff (no blocks; one mountain)
entries.purpose: Shaivite temple representing Kailash, Shiva's cosmic mountain
parts: ~200,000 t of rock removed by hand
elephants and lions flanking the base
layout: a free-standing temple carved down into a basalt trench
100 m long by 60 wide and 32 high, all one cliff
approached through a two-storey gateway carved from the same rock
entries.found: one, at Ellora, Maharashtra, India; the masterpiece of the Ellora Caves complex
entries.notes: Entirely subtractive: start with a cliff, end with a temple. Took an estimated 100+ years; the largest monolithic rock-cut excavation in the world.

entries.name: Bet Giyorgis (Church of Saint George), Lalibela
materials: volcanic tuff (carved from living rock, monolithic)
entries.purpose: Christian church; New Jerusalem after Muslim conquest of the Holy Land
parts: Greek cross plan carved from a single block
stands in a deep pit accessed by trenches
interior tunnels join it to ten other rock-hewn churches
layout: a cross-shaped monolith sitting in a hand-dug courtyard pit
seen from above only; the most complete Lalibela church
surrounding rock left as trenches and pathways
entries.found: one, at Lalibela, Ethiopia; one of eleven rock-hewn churches in the town
entries.notes: Carved top-down; nobody knows how. Created after Saladin closed Jerusalem to Christian pilgrims; Ethiopia simply built its own Holy Land in the highlands.

entries.name: Great Mosque of Djenné
entries.purpose: Friday mosque; spiritual and civic heart of Djenné on the Bani floodplain
parts: three great minarets with conical pinnacles
18 buttress pilasters ending in ostrich eggs
projecting toron beams doubling as ladders (crépissage)
layout: a long prayer hall on a 91 m flood-proof platform
toron beams grid the three minaret faces
ostrich eggs crown each pillar; the town replasters it every year
entries.found: one, in Djenné, Mali; the largest mud-brick building in the world
entries.notes: Rebuilt every year in the crépissage festival; the annual mudding is a civic sacrament. Not permanent: a perpetual construction project on purpose.

entries.name: Great Zimbabwe (Great Enclosure)
entries.purpose: royal capital of the Kingdom of Zimbabwe; political and ceremonial center
parts: outer elliptical wall, ~250 m circumference, 11 m high
Conical Tower, 9 m high, 5.5 m diameter
layout: a ring of dry-stone walls around a royal compound on granite hills
the Conical Tower stands alone in the Great Enclosure
city of up to 18,000 at its peak
entries.found: one, near Masvingo, Zimbabwe, over 1,000 associated stone-walled sites exist
entries.notes: Name means 'stone houses'; gave the modern nation its name. Europeans refused to believe Africans built it — they were wrong.

entries.name: Serpent Mound
entries.era: c. 1070 CE (debated); older repairs c. 320 BCE possible
entries.purpose: effigy mound; likely ceremonial; summer solstice sunset alignment
parts: 411 m long winding serpent, seven coils
built on a meteorite-impact crater rim
layout: a snake 1.4 soccer-fields long laid out on a bluff
invisible from the ground; only aerial view shows the shape
east-facing head with the egg
entries.found: one, near Peebles, Ohio, USA
entries.notes: Visibility is the trick: ground level shows nothing; the shape only reads from above or from a hill tower. The game's 'you must be airborne to see it' moment.

entries.name: Uluru (Ayers Rock)
entries.purpose: sacred landmark of Anangu; site of creation stories (tjukurpa)
parts: inselberg 3.6 km long, rising 348 m above the plain
a further 2.5 km of rock extends underground
kata tjuta rock domes 30 km away
layout: a single vast rounded dome of red rock in flat red desert
glows orange-red at sunrise and sunset
perimeter walk about 10.6 km
entries.found: one, in the Red Centre of the Northern Territory, Australia
entries.notes: Not built; sung into being, in Anangu belief. Climbing was banned in 2019 at traditional owners' request. Natural, but as loaded as any temple.
